## Independent review of PR #219 (static review, tests not re-run)

**Verdict:** I found no gouge or false-acquittal paths. One BLOCKING defect is in the new refusal text.

### BLOCKING

1. **The refusal message has runs of literal spaces in it.** In `drill_reach.rs` around line 279, the `format!` string is a single source line. The `\` line continuations were lost, so about 22 spaces stay in the text in three places: after "stands", after "on that line at Z", and after "raise". The user sees `...behind the tip) stands                      27.000 mm out...`. The pins check substrings (`"27.000 mm out along its hole's line"`, `"inside the stock's radius 30.000 on that line"`), so they pass anyway. **Fix:** restore the `\` continuations, like the corner-radius refusal just below. Add one assert on the full sentence, or on `"stands 27.000 mm"` and `"at Z -22.000 to 22.000"`, so the spacing is pinned.

### Message accuracy (non-blocking, worth tightening while there)

- It says "the stock's radius N" even when the material is the part. In the boss pin, the block at x40 is part material. It is also a coordinate along the hole line, not a radius. "inside the material standing N mm out along that line" would be accurate.
- "raise the clearance above the end face" does not help a holder that meets the face on its own station. It is copied from the swing refusal. For this case, "use a longer tool or a slimmer holder, or turn the bar to size first" fits.

### False-acquittal hunt: what I checked and found sound

- **Classifying "on one station".** The kernel (`motion/drilling/cross.rs`) only emits X/Y poses, set to exactly `-dir`. A move counts as on-station only when the pose is an exact unit X/Y vector (1e-9) and it does not move both along and across the line (`du <= 1e-6 || dw <= 1e-6`).
  - A quarter-turn traverse always has both `du` and `dw` non-zero: the hop radius is outside the bar, and the other station's mouth coordinate is inside it. So it falls back to the corner radius.
  - A rapid between two holes on the same face at different Y/Z keeps `du = 0`. The tube is widened by half the slide on each side in both W and Z. That is the bounding box of the holder's swept cylinder, which is conservative.
  - A move with along-line and Z components uses `min(u) + reach` as the face, with Z widened, which is also conservative.
  - A pose a little off axis cannot occur from this kernel. If it did, it would not pass the 1e-9 test and would fall back.
- **Opposite-station detour.** The leg above the end face, `p0 -> p1` at `z_top`, carries the new pose. It moves only along the line, so it is classified as on-station. The tube at `z_top ± hr` reads exactly what the old band check read at the same Z band: with material in the band it refuses, with none it passes. Neither check models the pose flip itself, so this is no regression.
- **Tube size.** The holder is a cylinder of radius `hr` about the line, so it fits inside the square tube of half-width `hr` in W and Z. The tube is unbounded outward, so `holder_len` and everything behind the face are covered. Clear means the face's outward coordinate is at or beyond the outermost material in the tube. That is correct, because the holder occupies only `u >= face`.
- **`None` means no material.** The tube is unbounded along its line, so a closed solid that meets it must cross it with a facet. Non-finite vertices are dropped, the same way the old `band_r` dropped them.
- **Part material (a boss).** `station::material` merges the part and the stock, each shifted into the spindle frame. Each keeps its own sagitta, so no fake curvature appears across the two meshes. The boss pin (block to x40 inside the Ø44 footprint) refuses at 40.000.
- **Round bar.** `tube_reach` substitutes the circumscribed `sqrt(raw^2 - edge^2)` at the tube edge nearest the axis, with `raw` the widest vertex radius over all Z. That bound holds for every point in the tube. When `face_or_circ` takes the mesh reading instead (a stepped bar whose flange sets `raw`), the curved facets' sagitta slabs, at `(w/2)tan(theta/2)` (more than the true sagitta), keep it an upper bound. `entry()` uses the same rule.
- **Rapids and feeds.** Every move is checked, whatever its kind.
- **Start and end of a hole.** The plunge and retract move along the line only, so the face is read at the innermost tip plus `reach`, which is the floor. The first move (start point to `r_d`) carries hole 0's pose and stays on station. The final exit rapid also stays on station.
- **Frame.** `cross_holder` runs on the chain before it is shifted back to the world, and `material` shifts the world facets by the same origin, so the two are consistent.

Not approved and not merged. The geometry is clean, and the PR is merge-ready once the message spacing is fixed and pinned.

Review blocker fixed in 55fadde:
- The refusal string's line continuations are restored, so the stray spaces are gone.
- It now says "inside material N mm out on that line", since it's not a radius and part material counts.
- The advice is now "use a tool with a longer reach, or turn or face the material back first".
- A test asserts the spaced text "stands 27.000 mm out".
drill_reach 6, drilling_cross_box 7, drilling_cross_holder 2, lathe_cross_drill 5 and lib drill_reach 8 all pass; clippy is clean.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.85 (rough estimate from size: 366 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
